title: ChipAlign: Instruction Alignment in Large Language Models for Chip Design via Geodesic Interpolation
problem: Chip-specific LLMs like ChipNeMo lack instruction alignment capability, limiting their ability to follow explicit human directives and serve as practical assistant chatbots for hardware design engineers.
motivation: Combining general instruction-aligned LLMs with domain-specific chip expertise addresses a critical practical bottleneck in deploying LLMs for hardware design automation.
method: ChipAlign merges two trained AI models—one designed to follow instructions, one trained on chip-design knowledge—by blending their internal weights without any retraining. It uses geodesic interpolation (finding the mathematically optimal path through the high-dimensional space where weights live) to fuse these models smoothly. The result is a single model that has both strong instruction-following ability and chip-design expertise.
key_novelty: Geodesic interpolation through weight space lets you merge two models without retraining, simultaneously achieving instruction alignment and chip-design expertise.
contributions: Novel geodesic interpolation strategy for weight-space model merging without training
26.6% improvement on IFEval instruction-following benchmark for chip LLMs
3.9% improvement on OpenROAD QA and 8.25% on production-level chip QA benchmarks

metrics.accuracy: 26.6% IFEval improvement, 3.9% OpenROAD QA, 8.25% production QA

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation limited to QA and instruction-following benchmarks without full design flow integration.
primary_theme: LLM instruction alignment for chip design
